title: Vishnu Sahasranamam Lyrics with Meaning: Verses 75-76
desc: Vishnu Sahasranamam verses 75 to 76 in Sanskrit with a simple English meaning and how to chant them: 'सद्गतिः सत्कृतिः सत्ता सद्भूतिः सत्परायणः'.
alt: Lord Vishnu, Vishnu Sahasranamam verses 75 to 76 with meaning
caption: Vishnu Sahasranamam, verses 75 to 76.
intro: **Vishnu Sahasranamam** is the thousand names of Lord Vishnu, taught by Bhishma to Yudhishthira in the Mahabharata. This post gives **verses 75 to 76** with the Sanskrit text and a plain English meaning, so you can chant with understanding.
takeaways: The verses here open with **सद्गतिः सत्कृतिः सत्ता सद्भूतिः सत्परायणः**.
Read the Sanskrit slowly, then the meaning, then chant once more.
Thursday and Ekadashi are the days most families keep for Vishnu Sahasranamam.
A short daily portion is better than a rushed full reading.

p: Read the lines aloud, one breath for each half of a verse:
**सद्गतिः सत्कृतिः सत्ता सद्भूतिः सत्परायणः । शूरसेनो यदुश्रेष्ठः सन्निवासः सुयामुनः ॥** **भूतावासो वासुदेवः सर्वासुनिलयोऽनलः । दर्पहा दर्पदो दृप्तो दुर्धरोऽथापराजितः ॥**

The refuge of the good, the good deed and pure being is he. Noble glory and the final shelter of saints is that God of gods. Shurasena, the best of the Yadus, the home of all, who played on the banks of the Yamuna. The home of all beings, Vasudeva is he. The support of every life and the fire is that God of gods. He crushes pride, grants dignity, shines with splendour, none can bear him, none can defeat him.
Light a lamp, sit facing east and chant these verses once, then read the meaning silently. Many families take two verses a day and finish the full text in a little under two months.
The names do not need a long ritual. What matters is steady practice, a clear pronunciation and a calm mind.

ul: Thursdays, the day of Vishnu and the planet Jupiter.
Early morning after a bath, or in the evening at the lamp.

faq.q: What do Vishnu Sahasranamam verses 75 to 76 mean?
faq.a: The refuge of the good, the good deed and pure being is he. Noble glory and the final shelter of saints is that God of gods. Shurasena, the best of the Yadus, the home of all, who played on the banks of the Yamuna. The home of all beings, Vasudeva is he. The support of every life and the fire is that God of gods. He crushes pride, grants dignity, shines with splendour, none can bear him, none can defeat him.
**Bhishma** taught it to Yudhishthira on the field of Kurukshetra, as told in the Anushasana Parva of the Mahabharata.

faq.q: Can I chant a few verses a day instead of the whole text?
faq.a: Yes. A small daily portion with the meaning understood is a common and accepted way to learn it.

note: The Sanskrit is the traditional text. The English is our own plain rendering of the meaning.
